title: Cook's first voyage in the Endeavour, 1768–71
summary: Sent to watch the transit of Venus from Tahiti, the Endeavour took on Tupaia, a Raʻiatean priest and navigator, who drew a chart of the Pacific and spoke for the ship in Aotearoa. She then charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, and every landfall was also a meeting with the people already there.

events.label: Point Venus: the transit of Venus
events.source: Wikipedia, First voyage of James Cook
events.text: The voyage's stated purpose. The transit of Venus was watched from a fort and observatory built at what is now called Point Venus, in Matavai Bay.

events.label: Raʻiatea: Cook claims the Society Islands
events.source: Wikipedia, First voyage of James Cook
events.text: The Endeavour anchored at Raʻiatea on 20 July 1769, and Cook claimed the Society Islands for Great Britain. For Tupaia it was home: he was born near Haʻamanino Harbour and was a priest of the Taputapuātea marae.

events.label: Tupaia's chart of the Pacific
events.text: Asked about the islands round about, Tupaia drew a chart with Cook, Banks and several officers, from 15 August 1769, aboard the Endeavour after she left the Society Islands. It shows 130 islands within a radius of 2,000 miles, 74 of which he could name. Later research reads it as the mark of navigational knowledge across much of the Polynesian Triangle. The mark stands at Raʻiatea, his home island, not where the sheet was drawn.

events.label: Tūranganui-a-Kiwa: the first landing, told twice
events.source: Gisborne Herald; Department of Conservation; NZ Herald
events.text: From the ship: Cook's party landed on the shore of Poverty Bay, and a man came down to the water with a spear. After two warning musket shots Cook's crew shot him dead. From the shore: he was Te Maro, a highly esteemed leader of Ngāti Oneone; he and three warriors went down to meet the strangers, and one historian says nobody will ever know whether he was performing a challenge, a wero, or confronting the unknown. Tupaia stayed aboard that day; on the next, a second landing found he could speak with the people and be understood. Nine Māori were killed in the encounters of those two days. On 2 October 2019 the British High Commissioner gave the Tūranga iwi a formal expression of regret for the violence of Cook's arrival.
events.doubt: Sources date the landing 8 or 9 October 1769, and an account has Cook's coxswain firing the shot that killed Te Maro.

events.label: Kamay: the Gweagal oppose the landing
events.text: Cook's party landed at Silver Beach on 29 April 1770. Two Gweagal men confronted them; Cook's party fired small shot and wounded one in the leg, spears were thrown, and a second round of shot sent the men away. A shield said to have been dropped by a Gweagal warrior was taken to England by Banks.
events.doubt: In 2018 the anthropologist Nicholas Thomas concluded that the shield now in the British Museum is not the one taken at Botany Bay: its wood is red mangrove, which grows at least 500 kilometres to the north.

events.label: Endeavour Reef: the ship strikes coral
events.source: Wikipedia, First voyage of James Cook
events.text: The Endeavour grounded on a shoal of the Great Barrier Reef on 11 June 1770 and was got off after about 23 hours.

events.label: Waalumbaal Birri: the turtles and the peace
events.text: The Endeavour was repaired here, on the river the Guugu Yimithirr call Waalumbaal Birri. On 18 July Guugu Yimithirr men boarded and found turtles on deck; the turtles, as the heritage register tells it, had been taken from sacred breeding grounds without permission. They set fire to the grass round the crew's camp, and Cook fired a musket and hit a man. Peace was offered by the Guugu Yimithirr and accepted by the crew at Reconciliation Rocks on 19 July, an act the register links to the elder Ngamu Yarrbarigu and which is described as one of the first acts of reconciliation on Australian soil.

events.label: Possession Island: Cook claims the east coast
events.source: Wikipedia, First voyage of James Cook
events.text: Near Cape York, Cook claimed the whole eastern coast of Australia for Britain.

events.label: Batavia: the ship's company falls sick
events.source: Wikipedia, First voyage of James Cook
events.text: The Endeavour reached the Dutch port of Batavia in October 1770 for repairs. Seven men died there, among them Tupaia and Taiata, and 23 more on the passage home.
